subject: Quiet window & fallback network plan for Brightwell private upgrade
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightwell.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Quiet window & fallback network plan for Brightwell private upgrade

Hi Laura / Brightwell Ops,

Following our call yesterday I’m proposing a tight maintenance window for the private cluster upgrade next week and want to align on network fallback and rollback commitments before we schedule. Key asks from our side:

- Preferred quiet window: Wed 2026-11-18 02:00–04:00 UTC (narrow 2h) — is that workable for you?
- Confirmation of any external BGP/peering changes that Brightwell will permit during the window. We’d like pre-approved BGP failover to the backup transit if health checks fail.
- Primary contact for Brightwell during the window (phone + escalation after-hours).

Planned scope: pin current runtime to v1.14.3 for customer instances, apply OS and runtime kernel micropatches on hosts that host the private inference runtime, run canary on 2 nodes, then roll to remaining nodes in slices. Rollback plan is snapshot-based + config re-pin.

We’ll attach the playbook and canary results for your review; please flag any policy or audit concerns (e.g., snapshot retention, KMS handling for model keys).

If the proposed window works, I’ll send a calendar invite and call owners.

Thanks,
Rafael
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: maintenance-playbook-v1.2.pdf, preflight-checklist.md

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightwell.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightwell Ops <ops@brightwell.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quiet window & fallback network plan for Brightwell private upgrade

Rafael—

Thanks. Wed 2026-11-18 02:00–04:00 UTC is acceptable. A few clarifications from Brightwell side:

- We need a 20-minute read-only period before any KV cache eviction that might surface stale behavior to callers.
- Can you confirm expected user-facing downtime for the inference API (if any) and SLA credit thresholds?
- Our network team requests we do NOT do BGP withdraws unless there is a verified host-level failure; prefer route-metric adjustment to shift traffic first.

Primary contact will be me (mobile: +1-415-555-0199) and our on-call is ops@brightwell.com. If you need any signed approvals prior to the window, we’ll process on DocuSign.

Laura
Head of Infrastructure
Brightwell Financial

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightwell.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T13:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quiet window & fallback network plan for Brightwell private upgrade

Laura / team —

Thanks for the constraints. Below is the operational plan (high level) and rollback triggers. I attached the playbook and the canary spreadsheet with the last run (attached).

Operational plan (ordered):
1) Preflight (48–24h out): full snapshot of control-plane state (etcd/kv pairs), export model pin metadata, KMS audit check. Preflight checklist (preflight-checklist.md) to be signed off by Brightwell Ops.
2) Quiet window start: notify routing/observability, set read-only for non-essential writes for 20 minutes.
3) Canary slice: select two nodes in a single AZ; pin runtime binary to v1.14.3 and run simulated traffic (synthetic traces). Validate tail-latency, token-per-second, and accuracy regression thresholds documented in the playbook.
4) Gradual roll: roll by pod/host slices with KV cache warmup and prefix caching. Observe 15m steady state between slices.
5) Network fallback: We will attempt route-metric adjustment first (as Brightwell requested). If health checks show >3 consecutive failed pings and API 5xx spike >1.5x baseline for 5m, we will initiate BGP withdraw to force failover.

Rollback triggers (immediate):
- Canary failure: any accuracy regression >1% or sustained 5xx >0.5% during canary -> immediate rollback to v1.14.2 and restore snapshot.
- Network instability during rollout: packet loss >2% for >10m -> pause and investigate; if unresolved after 30m -> rollback.

Rollback procedure (short):
- Re-pin runtime to prior version via orchestration template, trigger config reapply, restore node snapshots for affected slices, flush KV cache only after snapshot restore and sanity check.
- Post-rollback audit: collect logs, open INF rollback ticket, postmortem within 48h.

Owners:
- O/T (ops owner): Rafael Mendes (Redwood)
- Network liaison (Brightwell): Laura Chen
- Canary owner: Karthik Iyer (Redwood)

Please review the attached playbook and canary-results; call out anything missing for compliance or audit.

Attachments: maintenance-playbook-v1.2.pdf, canary-results-20261110.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightwell.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quiet window & fallback network plan for Brightwell private upgrade

Quick notes:

- I validated the canary traffic profile; we should add one micro-burst test at 2x peak to ensure KV cache pruning behavior. I added that to the canary sheet.
- Network ask: we will need temporary route-map permission for metric bumping from Brightwell to avoid manual telco calls mid-window. Laura — can you pre-authorize a single metric-adjust operation (readable in the playbook) that your team can revoke post-window?
- Suggest we run a short preflight on Tue 2026-11-17 22:00–22:30 UTC (no changes, just a canary run and verification). Can someone from Brightwell Ops join that 30m slot?

If preflight succeeds, rolling on Wed looks good to me.

-Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightwell.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quiet window & fallback network plan for Brightwell private upgrade

Laura / team —

Thanks — summary and agreed next steps:

1) Window confirmed: 2026-11-18 02:00–04:00 UTC.
2) Brightwell to pre-authorize route-metric adjustment for a single automated metric bump (documented in maintenance-playbook-v1.2.pdf). BGP withdraw is permitted only after automated health-check escalation.
3) Preflight check: Tue 2026-11-17 22:00–22:30 UTC — Redwood will run non-invasive canary; Brightwell Ops to observe and sign-off.
4) Contacts: Laura (mobile +1-415-555-0199) and ops@brightwell.com. Redwood incident bridge owner: Rafael Mendes.
5) Attachments shared (playbook, canary results, preflight checklist). Rafael to create calendar invites and post the DocuSign request for the maintenance approval.

If no objections, I will send invites and the DocuSign link by EOD.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
